Team / Elena —

I reviewed BigHealth's annotations and attached a redlined DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.pdf) with a suggested compromise for backup/DR carve-outs. Key proposal below (draft clause):

"Backup and Disaster Recovery. Notwithstanding any other provision, Customer Data that is durably stored in encrypted backup or disaster recovery systems may be retained for the limited purpose of disaster recovery, data restoration, or compliance with legal obligations. Such backup copies will: (a) be stored in encrypted, access-controlled systems; (b) not be used for product development, analytics, or other operational purposes; (c) be retained for no longer than twelve (12) months from the date of the backup unless a legally binding hold is in place; and (d) be deleted or rendered unrecoverable within ninety (90) days after the expiration of the retention period or conclusion of any legally binding hold, subject to reasonable technical constraints.

For legal holds, Redwood will maintain reasonable internal processes to isolate backup copies and will notify Customer of any restoration or access to data subject to a hold. Access to isolated backup material will be limited to personnel with a documented business need and will be logged.

Rationale: the 12-month window balances BigHealth's need for reliable recovery with our operational constraints; the 90-day purge after hold expiration acknowledges technical recovery windows while limiting indefinite retention. If BigHealth needs a longer period for specific regulatory reasons, we can consider a scoped carve-out tied to the relevant dataset and stricter access controls.

If this looks acceptable, Jordan please confirm we can propose these exact lines back to Elena and request DocuSign for execution.

—Karthik
